title: Vendor escalation becomes a ticket graveyard
source_story: User-provided fictional owner stories in this conversation; opening narrative below is a faithful condensed adaptation, not a verbatim transcript.
business_context: Ten-person office network, Wi-Fi and general IT service provider.
owner_narrative: The internet provider wants wired tests; the application vendor wants logs. Our notes rarely say where or when tests occurred. Second technicians repeat them. An access point replacement did not fix a meeting-room problem that returned during busy events. Waiting for vendor can last indefinitely.

evidence.description: A simulated test log omits load conditions.
A simulated vendor request remains unanswered.
A simulated closure note records only temporary restoration.

diagnoses.hypothesis: Evidence lacks reproducible context and escalations lose accountable ownership.
diagnoses.counterhypothesis: A supplier may have a real unresolved external defect; the service firm can manage evidence and communications without claiming to fix it.
diagnoses.confidence_policy: Qualitative case-world support only; requires fresh customer evidence before reuse.

interventions.process_first: Record test context, results and next vendor action; separate restored, monitoring and resolved states.
interventions.deterministic_and_assisted_automation: Build structured investigation timelines and vendor follow-up tasks; draft evidence packages with sensitive information removed.
interventions.rejected_default: Do not replace the whole service platform or deploy autonomous agents solely because the owner reports inefficiency.
interventions.selection_basis: Choose the least complex intervention addressing the supported handoff failure; compare added administration and integration burden.

requirements.statement: A workaround cannot automatically close the underlying investigation.
requirements.rationale: Evidence lacks reproducible context and escalations lose accountable ownership.

requirements.statement: Every waiting state has an owner and review date.
requirements.rationale: Evidence lacks reproducible context and escalations lose accountable ownership.

requirements.statement: Vendor evidence exports exclude credentials and unrelated customer data.
requirements.rationale: Evidence lacks reproducible context and escalations lose accountable ownership.

acceptance_tests.scenario_and_expected_result: A second technician sees prior conditions and results.
Recurrence under original load prevents confirmed-resolution status.

capability_boundary.proposed_extension: Structured technical investigation and supplier-case linking are additional capabilities.
capability_boundary.pricing: No price assigned; current rate card must not be extended by analogy.

evaluation.primary_metric_definition: Age of externally blocked incidents and repeated diagnostic effort; track recurrence after closure.
measurement_cautions: Use a stable denominator and comparable operating periods.
Record missingness and changed case mix.
Do not infer staff reductions from reclaimed task minutes.

implementation.baseline: Collect at least one representative operating cycle before rollout; for monthly billing or maintenance include the relevant full cycle. Extend sampling when volumes or seasonality make the sample unrepresentative.
implementation.scope: Start with one consenting customer group and the staff who own its handoffs; include a normal case and each listed exception.
sequence: Reconcile identities and existing obligations with the process owner.
Run the proposed rules in shadow mode; record disagreements and missed exceptions.
Approve a bounded live pilot only after requirements and exceptions have named owners.
Review outcome metrics, added administrative work and failure logs before expanding.
implementation.simulated_resolution: In this fictional case, MILO introduced the process change: Record test context, results and next vendor action; separate restored, monitoring and resolved states. The team adopted the proposed workflow for the pilot scope. Routine coordination became explicit; unresolved exceptions continued to require a person.
implementation.simulated_lesson: A supplier may have a real unresolved external defect; the service firm can manage evidence and communications without claiming to fix it.
implementation.rollback: Pause automated writes and notifications, retain the event log, export outstanding work and return to a named manual coordinator. Reconcile queued events before resuming to avoid duplicate actions.
implementation.go_no_go: Process owner reviews coverage of acceptance cases, unresolved critical failures, metric direction and staff workload. No fixed performance threshold is claimed without customer agreement.

open_questions: Supplier support windows and permissible diagnostic data vary by agreement.
